title: Minimum Path Sum
statement: You are given a rectangular grid of non-negative integers as a list of lists, where grid[r][c] is the toll charged for stepping on that cell. A walker begins on the top-left cell and wants to reach the bottom-right cell, moving only one cell right or one cell down at each step. The walker pays the toll of every cell they stand on, including both the starting and ending cells. Return the minimum total toll over all such walks. The grid always has at least one row and at least one column, so a valid walk always exists (a 1x1 grid costs exactly its single cell).
hints: For any cell, how could the walker have arrived there, and what is the cheapest cost of each way in?
Build a table dp[i][j] = cheapest total toll to reach cell (i, j); each interior cell is grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

Initialize dp[0][0] = grid[0][0], then fill the first row and first column as running prefix sums (each has only ONE way in), and only then sweep the interior with the min recurrence; answer is dp[m-1][n-1].
